rule: D042 condition 2; RUNBOOK 11; owner goal part-time / fail closed
summary: A failed nightly backup is visible only in systemctl status/journalctl: no OnFailure, no alert, no snapshot-age probe.
expected: A failed or missing backup reaches the operator without a login (Telegram, external monitor fail/silence, or a health probe of the newest snapshot age).
actual: trading-backup.service and trading-soak-backup.service have no OnFailure=; no code or heartbeat checks backup age; RUNBOOK 231 tells the operator to run systemctl status.
impact: Mainnet: the operational DB can be without a usable off-host copy for days or weeks, discovered only at restore time.
evidence: trading-backup.service:3-4 'a failed backup makes this oneshot unit fail visibly (systemctl status ...)'; grep -rn OnFailure deploy -> none; grep -i backup src/ops/health.py deploy/heartbeat.sh src/live/*.py -> none.
reproduction: Read the unit files and grep as above.
why_tests_miss: Tests check unit text and exit codes, not that a human is told.
recommendation: OnFailure= notify unit, or an external-monitor check pinged only on scheduled-OK, or a snapshot-age health probe.

summary: Backups cover PostgreSQL and rawdata only, once a day: the livestate (REST gate state, spill) and logs volumes are never backed up, and up to 24 h of live journal is lost on host loss; neither is documented as an RPO.
expected: Either the volumes are in the bundle or the loss and the post-restore procedure are documented; an RPO for the live journal chosen by the owner.
actual: backup mounts rawdata (ro) and backupdata only (269-274); livestate holds gate state, spill, liveness, held marker (213-215); timer OnCalendar 03:15 UTC daily.
impact: Mainnet: after restore the journal does not know the last day's approvals/orders/fills/reservations; gate state missing (fail-closed); spill lost; reliance on reconcile against Binance.
reproduction: Compare the backup service volumes with the volume list.
why_tests_miss: The restore drill compares restored and live DB at the same moment; it never models a loss long after the last backup.
recommendation: Document RPO and post-restore steps; more frequent dumps or WAL archiving once live; include the livestate spill.

summary: Nothing enforces a single live process: no instance lease or advisory lock in src/live, and deploy/compose-soak.sh accepts --profile live, which starts a second live in project trading-soak with the production .env.live keys and its own DB and gate state.
expected: A second live start for the same account refuses or holds (as the paper runtime does with INSTANCE_LEASE_HELD), plus a wrapper refusal and a runbook rule for restore/cutover.
actual: No lease (grep lease/lock/advisory in src/live and src -> none outside paper); live env file is not redirected per project (deploy/lib.sh:112); compose-soak.sh has no live rule; update.sh checks only its own project's live service.
impact: Mainnet: two protection coordinators/reconcilers and two REST weight budgets on one account, each blind to the other's journal; likely SAFE_MODE, possibly duplicate stops, cancels of the other's stop, or a ban.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:227-229; deploy/lib.sh:106-120; deploy/compose-soak.sh:1-40; deploy/update.sh:105-128; src/paper/runtime.py:144-146,379 (paper lease exists).
why_tests_miss: Tests pin per-service env lists and the soak down -v refusal, never a second live instance.
recommendation: PostgreSQL advisory lock/lease at live start; refuse the live profile in compose-soak.sh; runbook rule for restore and cutover.

summary: The shape layer misses several credential forms (bare API key, apiKey=, libpq password= kv, non-AKIA S3 key ids, ping URLs, dict-repr or base64 signatures); masking relies on the env/runtime value layer.
expected: Shapes cover the credential forms the project handles, independent of env naming.
actual: Probe: 18 of 28 cases leak, all either without a registered value or of low value (single-use signatures, upper-cased/truncated text, values < 8 chars).
impact: Defence-in-depth gap; no live leak found because the value layer and register_runtime_secret cover every main path checked.
recommendation: Add shapes for password= kv, apiKey=, API-key <alnum>, base64 signature=, 'signature': '...'.

rule: AGENTS.md secrets in env files mode 0600; RUNBOOK 22 .env.live mode 0600
summary: Only .env is installed and checked at mode 0600; .env.live (trade-capable Binance key, live bot token), .env.backup and .env.paper are hand-made and never mode-checked.
expected: The same mode check for the per-service secret files, at least .env.live.
actual: No script or runtime checks their mode; compose reads them with required: false.
impact: A world-readable .env.live exposes the live API key to other local accounts.
evidence: bootstrap.sh:559-563 (install -m 0600 .env, die if not 600); grep env.live deploy/*.sh -> comments only.
why_tests_miss: No test of per-service env file modes.
recommendation: Refuse at live start (or in a wrapper) when the live env file is group/other readable.

rule: least privilege (practice); intent of D-29 per-service split
summary: Collector, paper, live, backup and ops all connect as POSTGRES_USER, the superuser created by the official image.
expected: Per-service DB roles; superuser only for db-upgrade.
actual: One DATABASE_URL with the superuser for every service.
impact: A compromise of any container gives DB superuser (journal rewrite, COPY TO PROGRAM).
evidence: docker-compose.yml:66 DATABASE_URL built from POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_PASSWORD; :73-74 same role initialises postgres.
